name: Question 2
problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=3{x}^{2}y-{x}^{2}+2xy-3x.
$$

Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,2]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{1}≈[$ | $0.375$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-1}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}y-{x}^{2}+2xy-3x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}y-{x}^{2}+2xy-3x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6xy-2x+2y-3 \\ 3{x}^{2}+2x\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(6xy-2x+2y-3) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}+2x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(6xy-2x+2y-3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}+2x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6y-2 & 6x+2 \\ 6x+2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}6y-2 & 6x+2 \\ 6x+2 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}6xy-2x+2y-3 \\ 3{x}^{2}+2x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with
${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}6y-2 & 6x+2 \\ 6x+2 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}6xy-2x+2y-3 \\ 3{x}^{2}+2x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}6(2)-2 & 6(1)+2 \\ 6(1)+2 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}6(1)(2)-2(1)+2(2)-3 \\ 3(1)^{2}+2(1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}10 & 8 \\ 8 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{10\cdot 0-8\cdot 8}[\begin{aligned}0 & -8 \\ -8 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{64}[\begin{aligned}-40 \\ -38\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.375 \\ 1.406\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function f:Rn→R is

xn+1=xn−[Hf(xn)]−1∇f(xn),

where H(xn) and ∇f(xn) are the Hessian and gradient of f, respectively, evaluated at xn.

In our case, the gradient is

∇f(x)=[∂∂x(3x2y−x2+2xy−3x)∂∂y(3x2y−x2+2xy−3x)]=[6xy−2x+2y−33x2+2x],

and the Hessian is

Hf(x)=[∂∂x(6xy−2x+2y−3)∂∂x(3x2+2x)∂∂y(6xy−2x+2y−3)∂∂y(3x2+2x)]=[6y−26x+26x+20].

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

xn+1=xn−[6y−26x+26x+20]xn−1[6xy−2x+2y−33x2+2x]xn.

Starting with x0=[12], we have

x1=x0−[6y−26x+26x+20]x0−1[6xy−2x+2y−33x2+2x]x0=[12]−[6(2)−26(1)+26(1)+20]−1[6(1)(2)−2(1)+2(2)−33(1)2+2(1)]=[12]−[10880]−1[115]=[12]−110⋅0−8⋅8[0−8−810][115]=[12]+164[−40−38]≈[0.3751.406].
